subject: Claude Code parallel tabs 💻, DigUp local search 🔍, Gemini 4 Argon codi
intro: Parallelism is having a moment. Claude Code now runs multiple sessions side by side, Fork-and-Flush beats single-agent runs by 66% using parallel copies with wiped memory, and a local semantic search tool finds your files across all types at once. The pattern is clear: the next unlock isn't smarter models, it's smarter orchestration. Run more, reset often, stay in control. Turns out the best way to think harder is to think sideways .

news.headline: Claude Code desktop app now runs multiple coding sessions side by side
news.body: Claude Code's desktop app just got a serious upgrade for managing multiple tasks at once. Here's the deal. You can now run parallel sessions (think: multiple tasks happening at the same time, each in its own tab). Claude spins up a separate mini-session for each task, then reports results back to your main session when done. Your main thread stays clean and readable. This opens up running entire workflows in parallel without losing track of anything. Update the desktop app and start a new session to try it.
bullets: Live to-do list inside each session, so you always see what Claude is doing
A recap card appears when Claude needs your input, no digging required
Save folder setups, SSH hosts, or cloud configs as reusable environments
Use /btw to ask a side question in a new tab without interrupting your main session
One-click follow-up sessions from Claude's own suggestions

news.headline: Open-source macOS tool brings fully local semantic search to photos, audio, and code
news.body: Your Mac has always been bad at finding files. You remember the moment , not the filename. DigUp fixes that. DigUp is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that lets you search your files by describing what you remember. It runs Google DeepMind's EmbeddingGemma 2 entirely on your machine. No cloud. No account. No data leaving your laptop. The trick: it converts text, images, audio, and video into points in the same shared space. So one query can reach across all your file types at once. Here's what you can actually do: Hit Shift+Cmd+Space from anywhere. Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14+. One-time 865 MB model download, then fully offline.
bullets: Type "dog near water" and find the photo
Type "where they talk about sleep" and jump to that podcast minute
Type "payment declined error" and surface the right screenshot
Search your codebase by what a function does, not what it's called

news.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon, cutting bad code commits by 30% in production
news.body: Google just dropped Gemini 4 Argon , its most capable coding model yet, and it's already been battle-tested inside Google's own production codebases. The results? A 35% boost in code written by AI agents and 30% fewer bugs making it past code review. The big unlock here is output size. Argon can generate up to 1 million output tokens in one shot, up from 64K. Think of tokens as chunks of text. More tokens means the model can rewrite entire codebases, migrate legacy systems, or refactor hundreds of files without stopping mid-task. Real things it has already done: You can try it now in the Antigravity app or CLI , Google's agentic coding platform, if you're on AI Pro or Ultra. Install via curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh | bash, then run agy.
bullets: Helped Chrome engineers untangle a 40-million-line codebase, finishing months of work in weeks
Autonomously built a 3D Japanese pagoda in Blender using multi-agent looping
